# The replies the recorder sends the app over loopback as lines of text, as
# both sides speak them (0.26, 2026-11-01): not the handshake's answer (the
# recorder's nonce and MAC, bytes) nor the audio a capture (R) streams. One
# reply per line, four columns split by tabs:
#
#   command   the command byte(s) the app sends (Main.session)
#   app       source text in the app that reads this reply; "-" when the app
#             only logs or passes it on
#   recorder  source text in shellserver/src that writes it
#   example   a reply as the recorder builds it
#
# Both sides are written by hand and built apart: the app never compiles the
# recorder's sources. ProtocolTest (app) checks that each side still has its
# text and that the app's parsers read each example; the recorder's own test
# of the lines it builds comes with the 1.0 restructuring, which moves
# the formatting out of Main.java where daemon-tests can reach it.
# An installed app talks to whatever recorder is running, possibly an older
# one for days off Wi-Fi, so a reply changes only with both sides at once.
P	"PONG"	"PONG "	PONG 2 1a2b3c4d
Q	"BYE"	"BYE\n"	BYE
Q	"BUSY"	"BUSY\n"	BUSY
O	"OFF NOW"	"OFF NOW"	OFF NOW

O	"OFF TOO LATE"	"OFF TOO LATE"	OFF TOO LATE
